claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference potential with an MLIP trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Replacing the EAM reference with the proposed MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM approach.
The MLIP would be trained on a representative ab initio dataset containing both solid and liquid configurations.
The proposed method applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys containing several principal elements near their melting points.
The MLIP will capture short-range ordering effects present in the ab initio liquid.
The MLIP will capture medium-range ordering effects present in the ab initio liquid.
Capturing liquid ordering will make the MLIP potential-energy landscape more closely match the ab initio landscape.
Training on an extensive and diverse ab initio dataset will allow the MLIP to represent the wide range of atomic arrangements in the liquid.
Better representation of liquid atomic arrangements will enhance phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce discrepancies along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The reduction in integration-path mismatch is expected to be substantial.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will produce more reliable free-energy calculations.
TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials exhibit notable integration-path mismatches because of limited configurational diversity.
The proposed approach may be less effective at compositional extremes.
The proposed approach may be less effective at temperatures where other phenomena dominate the thermodynamics.
The quantitative improvement and robustness across alloy compositions and extreme conditions are uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing EAM- and MLIP-referenced thermodynamic-integration calculations against fully converged ab initio free-energy benchmarks.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in path-mismatch error with the MLIP would falsify the hypothesis.
